Subject: Follow-up: Logging & redaction controls — recap + next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and an outline of next steps so your security team can review:

1) Key requirements you mentioned
- No PII (name, SSN, account numbers) persisted in request/response logs
- Ability to redact/mask headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Trace-Id) and body fields (payment_info, ssn, email)
- Data residency: logs stored in us-east-1 only for pilot
- Retention target: 90 days for request/response logs, 365 days for audit metadata

2) What we said we could provide
- Field-level redaction (configurable regex + schema-aware)
- Header scrubbing rules and configurable header whitelist
- Per-route logging toggle (enable/disable request/response logs)
- Exportable redaction proof (sample scrubbed logs + redaction rules)

3) Action items / next steps
- I’ll send a concise tech write-up showing sample log lines before/after redaction and our deploy options (attached). (Marcus to provide sample snippets)
- Alex to share security questionnaire owners and any doc links (SOC 2 contact + retention policy).
- Schedule a short follow-up w/ your security team next week.

Attachments: SLA_Redaction_Controls.pdf (redaction approach + config options)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus in for the technical details.

—

Marissa — thanks for the quick summary, that matches our notes. A couple clarifying Qs from our security team before we loop them in:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood can remove or mask trace IDs entirely from stored logs? Our tracing IDs are considered sensitive because they can be correlated across systems.
- For headers, will the Authorization header always be stripped by default, or is that configured per-integration?
- Do you have an example of a request/response pair pre- and post-redaction so we can validate the redaction rules?

We prefer sample artifacts (snippets + diagram) we can hand to the SOC reviewer. Once we have that, we’ll schedule a 30-min call with our security lead (cc’d). Also, for the pilot we will need logs kept in us-east-1 only and retention capped at 90 days.

Alex

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Logging & redaction controls — sample logs + options

Alex — copying the technical details below and attaching a small diagram that shows where redaction happens in the request path (redaction-diagram.png).

Short answers to your Qs:
- Trace IDs: we can be configured to either (A) remove trace IDs from persisted logs, (B) hash them with a per-customer salt, or (C) keep them in ephemeral in-memory traces only (not written to disk). Removal or hashing can be applied globally or per-route.
- Authorization header: default behavior is to redact Authorization and Cookie headers from persisted logs. You can supply an allowlist of headers that are kept.

Sample before/after (simplified):

--- request (raw) ---
POST /api/v1/transactions HTTP/1.1
Host: api.fintechco.com
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJI...
X-Trace-Id: 6f1a2b3c-9d4e-4f5a-8abc-0123456789ab
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "user_id": "user_12345",
  "email": "alice@example.com",
  "payment_info": {"card_number": "4111111111111111", "expiry": "12/26"}
}

--- persisted log (after redaction rules) ---
POST /api/v1/transactions
Host: api.fintechco.com
Authorization: <REDACTED>
X-Trace-Id: <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "user_id": "user_12345",
  "email": "<REDACTED_EMAIL>",
  "payment_info": {"card_number": "<REDACTED_CARD>"}
}

Notes on implementation:
- Redaction uses a combination of JSON-path rules and regex patterns (we attach a starter ruleset).
- We also support schema-driven redaction where sensitive fields indicated in your OpenAPI can be automatically masked.
- Logs can be written to a customer-owned S3 bucket in the us-east-1 region (for Private/Dedicated) or to our segregated us-east-1 logging store for hosted pilots. Retention is configurable per-customer/route.

Attachment: redaction-diagram.png (shows redaction at ingress prior to storage)
Sample attachments: SLA_Redaction_Controls.pdf (policy)

Happy to join the security call — propose Wed 2026-03-11 10:00am PT if that works.

—
